desc: Parse input: H, W, X, start (P,Q) (convert to 0-indexed), and the H×W grid of strengths as Python ints.

Initialize T = S[P][Q], a visited boolean grid marking the start cell, and a min-heap seeded with the start cell's 4 neighbors (strength, row, col), marking them visited when pushed to avoid duplicates.
Implement the greedy loop: pop the minimum-strength frontier entry; if s*X < T, absorb (T += s) and push all unvisited 4-neighbors of that cell into the heap, marking them visited; else break.

Justify termination correctness in a comment: heap order guarantees the popped slime is the weakest candidate; if it fails the strict inequality, every remaining frontier slime also fails, and no future absorptions are possible.
Handle edge cases: X=1 (condition s < T, still works with s*1 < T), single-cell grids, and large values (Python ints avoid overflow; s*X can be up to ~10^21 which is fine).
Print final T to stdout, with fast input reading (sys.stdin.buffer.read) for up to 250,000 cells.
Implement solve(): parse input with sys.stdin.buffer.read, run the Prim-like greedy (min-heap frontier, absorb while s*X < T, mark visited on push), print final T.
Verify mentally against samples: sample 1 → 28, sample 2 → 5, sample 3 → 1343.
